title: Bounded traversal of gate arguments
statement: Let $C$ be a family of finite acyclic Boolean circuits, fix natural numbers $n,i,B$, a Boolean parameter $\ell$, and a gate $g$ of the circuit for input length $n$. Suppose the gate at index $V-n$ is $g$, $n\le V$, and $V+1\le B$. For every choice of natural numbers $d,U,k,W,K$ such that $U+d=V$, $k\le i$, $W\le B$, $K=k+|E|$, and $K\le B$, where $E$ is the encoding of the indices in $[U,U+d)$ that occur among the arguments of $g$, the emission property holds for $E$ starting from control state $aL$, registers $(k,V,U,W)$, and no answer. Its postcondition is that the resulting configuration has control state $gS$, registers $(K,V+1,V,W')$, and no answer for some $W'\le B$.
hypotheses_covered: The gate at index $V-n$ in the circuit for length $n$ is $g$.
For all $d,U,k,W,K$: $U+d=V$, $k\le i$, $W\le B$, $K=k+|E|$, and $K\le B$, where $E$ encodes the indices in the indicated interval that are arguments of $g$.
